name: Hindustan Media Ventures Ltd
title: Hindustan Media Ventures Ltd - 533217 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Print-led HMVL Q2 FY27: revenue up 5% to INR 502 cr and EBITDA up 26% to INR 88 cr, with no capacity or capex signals and flat circulation; radio and digital shrinking after station exits.

triggers.label: Newsprint costs flattened, peak view
triggers.quote: they've flattened at a certain level. We are not seeing any downward impetus at this point in time, but I believe they've already peaked out.

triggers.label: Print ad revenue up on share and DAVP
triggers.quote: we managed to consolidate a little bit, so we've got those volume gains. Also, if you remember, the industry got a certain DAVP price increase last year.

triggers.label: Radio loss-making stations surrendered
triggers.quote: whatever were the loss-making stations or frequencies, we have since surrendered to the government. And hence, we are a smaller network

red_flags.label: Ad-for-equity liabilities INR 555 cr, counter-entry unclear
red_flags.quote: there is no clear-cut INR 555 cr anywhere which we can find.

red_flags.label: Unallocated segment loss recurring
red_flags.quote: This is a consistent number across quarters.

evasions.quote: I can neither confirm nor deny, but I'll tell you very clearly that our Board is running the affairs of the Company.
Now that activity, the government still hasn't come back to us.

summary.headline: HT Media Group consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue rose 5% YoY to INR 502 cr, with EBITDA up 26% to INR 88 cr despite a 20-day festive shift.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 5% YoY to INR 502 cr and EBITDA rose 26% to INR 88 cr, lifting EBITDA margin to 17% from 15%. PAT reached INR 39 cr versus a margin of 4% a year earlier, and net cash stood at INR 930 cr. Print drove the quarter with operating revenue up 8% to INR 386 cr, while Radio and Digital revenues fell 23% and 30% YoY, reflecting station surrenders and a leaner digital portfolio. Management flagged newsprint and rupee depreciation as margin pressures and said the Diwali festive revenue shifted into Q3.

financial_highlights.change: margin about 9%; first positive after many quarters

segments.name: Print
segments.commentary: Operating revenue INR 386 cr (+8%), English +5%, Hindi +11%, driven by ad volume gains and government (DAVP) pricing; EBITDA nearly flat (-6%) on newsprint costs and festive shift. Circulation revenue flat at INR 54 cr.

segments.name: Radio
segments.commentary: Operating revenue INR 25 cr (-23%) after surrendering loss-making stations; operating EBITDA INR 2 cr (about 9% margin), first positive in many quarters. Management awaits government license fee revision for further profitability step-up.

segments.name: Digital
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 28 cr (-30% YoY) on a leaner portfolio; operating EBITDA about INR 1 cr, breakeven to slightly positive, with modest sequential improvement.

segments.name: Unallocated
segments.commentary: Corporate costs, auditor fees, KMP remuneration and mark-to-market movements on investments; loss of INR 12.37 cr.

guidance_outlook: No forward-looking guidance given; management reiterated a cautionary statement.
Newsprint prices have flattened at a high level; management believes they have peaked but gave no timing for decline.
Radio: management expects no return to losses, but says profitability will rise substantially only after the government revises the license fee structure, which has not yet happened.
Management expects festive-season revenue to be captured in Q3 FY27.
capex_capacity: Radio network rationalised by surrendering loss-making stations; the company now operates a smaller network.
Print copy count held flat; management said it will not add copies without a specific need given high newsprint costs.
Ongoing AFE (Ad for Equity) investments of INR 25 cr, INR 13.51 cr and INR 50 cr were approved at the board meeting, per management.
demand_pricing: Print ad growth came from market-share consolidation in Hindi and English markets plus a DAVP price increase industry-wide last year, primarily from government advertising.
Variable (direct) costs rose significantly YoY as rates increased; growth is price-led rather than volume-led.
Employee costs at consolidated level fell to about INR 95 cr from INR 99 cr QoQ and INR 105 cr YoY, attributed to group-wide cost rationalisation of indirect costs.
Rupee depreciation and global freight rates were cited as pressures on newsprint costs.

qa_highlights.question: What drove 5% English and 10%+ Hindi ad revenue growth, and does it hold for both?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited market-share consolidation in both markets and DAVP government ad pricing increase; Diwali shift of 20 days limited growth. Confirmed it holds for both English and Hindi.

qa_highlights.question: Why was circulation revenue not disclosed, and are copy counts rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Circulation revenue is flat at INR 54 cr (Hindi INR 39 cr) and copies are flat; management will not boost copies unnecessarily given high newsprint costs.

qa_highlights.question: Is newsprint cost relief coming?
qa_highlights.answer: Costs have flattened at elevated levels; management believes they have peaked but cannot forecast when they will decline.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs fall YoY and QoQ at consolidated level, and why did HMVL costs rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Group-wide cost rationalisation of indirect costs including people; HMVL variations reflect one-off reversals and timing differences.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR 555 cr in other financial liabilities (sundry deposits) and its counter-entry?
qa_highlights.answer: These are advances received under Ad-for-Equity arrangements; the asset side sits in non-current investments but not as an exact one-to-one match, as settlement depends on ad burn.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company in discussion with a large shareholder who has about 10% stake, and will capital allocation change after OTTplay stopped?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed ongoing conversations with a substantial shareholder but declined to comment on style; no capital allocation decisions are pending and any would be brought to the board and disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for Radio profitability and whether write-offs are complete; what drives the unallocated loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Radio will not slip back into losses and will not consume further cash, but a big profitability jump needs a license fee revision. Unallocated INR 12.37 cr covers corporate costs, director fees and mark-to-market changes, and is consistently reported.

risks_watch: Newsprint and rupee-driven cost pressure on Print margins, with no firm timing for relief.
Government decision on Radio license fee structure, which management says is needed for a meaningful profit step-up.
Festive-season revenue shift into Q3 FY27 makes the Q3 comparison lumpy.
Ad-for-Equity arrangements create INR 555 cr of financial liabilities, settled through ad burn and not one-to-one with investments.
Activist-style engagement from a shareholder holding close to 10%; capital allocation direction unclear.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the profit recovery and cash position, but evasive on capital allocation, the shareholder dialogue, and newsprint timing. Management declined to give forward guidance and repeatedly deflected questions on circulation and unallocated costs.
key_quotes: As we enter the festive quarter, the Company remains focused on strengthening its core businesses and maintaining financial discipline.
Now copies, we are in a very good position relative to our competition on a market-by-market basis.
Now once that happens, the profitability and the economics of the Radio business will change substantially.

adds.what: Radio network reduced by surrendering loss-making stations (shrinking, not adding capacity)

growth.why: No forward guidance was given; management reiterated a cautionary statement, and Q2 growth (revenue +5%, EBITDA +26%) was driven by print pricing (DAVP) and share gains, while radio and digital shrank via station surrenders and a leaner portfolio.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA margin rose to 17% from 15% and EBITDA grew 26% to INR 88 cr, but management flagged newsprint and rupee pressure with no timing for relief, and Radio uplift awaits a license fee revision.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Radio network shrank via station surrenders and print copy count is held flat, with management refusing to add copies without a specific need given high newsprint costs.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Growth is price-led rather than volume-led: print operating revenue rose 8% to INR 386 cr while circulation revenue was flat at INR 54 cr and copies are flat, and Radio (-23%) and Digital (-30%) shrank.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Board approved AFE investments of INR 25 cr, INR 13.51 cr and INR 50 cr, but no new capacity or utilisation level was disclosed, so a fresh capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No forward guidance was given and management only reiterated a cautionary statement.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged newsprint and rupee-driven cost pressure with no timing for relief, and the Q3 festive shift makes the comparison lumpy.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new products, brands or launches were discussed on the call.

rows.label: Radio license fee revision
rows.why: Management says Radio profitability will rise substantially only after the government revises the license fee structure, which has not happened yet; Radio EBITDA is only INR 2 cr on INR 25 cr revenue.

rows.label: Festive revenue shift into Q3 FY27
rows.why: Management expects Diwali festive-season revenue, which shifted out of Q2 (20-day festive shift), to be captured in Q3 FY27.

rows.label: Substantial shareholder (~10%) engagement
rows.why: Management confirmed ongoing conversations with a substantial shareholder holding about 10% but gave no capital allocation decisions; any would be taken to the board and disclosed.

tone.note: Management was confident on the profit recovery (EBITDA +26%, margin 17%) and net cash of INR 930 cr, but was evasive on capital allocation, the shareholder dialogue and newsprint timing; analysts pushed on ad growth durability, circulation and unallocated costs.
